findings.text: follow-on: test_every_add_dir_is_bound_writable_or_outside_every_sealed_path is a second copy, verbatim in assertion and name, of tests/test_a_fenced_codex_review_names_only_writable_roots.py:186, the file that owns that rule, and the new copy is the weaker of the two: its local _sealed_destinations at :69-70 reads only --ro-bind destinations while the owner's copy also collects --tmpfs paths, so a path the argv masks with --tmpfs and also names writable would redden the owner's assertion and pass this one; the genuine addition is the fixture's ambient node-tmp root, which belongs as an added case beside the owner.

follow-on: the follow_ons bullet cites logs/head_suite3.txt as holding the stopped widened-population attempt, but head_suite3.txt is the completed narrow arm (1 failed, 122 passed in 181.59s, EXIT=1) and no log in the run directory records the 116-file arm or its 4%-after-ten-minutes claim, so a reader checking whether the widened population was measured is pointed at a finished run and the unmeasured claim carries no receipt.

follow-on: the exclude_slash_tmp override is conditional on the read-only tier, so the sibling branch at :1319-1320 still returns --sandbox workspace-write with no override; codex's own workspace-write policy adds the node temp root and protects a .git inside every root it holds, which is the mechanism this node proved, so a fenced codex launch at the workspace-write tier meets the same /tmp/.git refusal on a sealed /tmp; no role or host config in ~/.config/reckon declares such a run today, so the gap is latent rather than live.
